transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time to discuss the proposed eighth-grade makerspace program. As you know, I'll be making the final authorization decision, but before I do, I want to gather input from each of you based on your areas of expertise. We're looking at a program with 24 students meeting twice a week during the spring semester, using soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter, with one STEM teacher supervising. I'd like to hear from each of you about any considerations or concerns related to implementation from your respective roles. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag an important safety finding before we go further. I completed my room-safety review this week, and it found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students. Additionally, any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers of 24 students and one supervising adult, so those will need to be revised before authorization.

I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a technology compliance issue with the draft program. I confirmed with the district technology office that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage. The approved workflow requires an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan. However, the draft program still instructs students to use cloud-based computer-aided design files, and I have not yet replaced that cloud-storage instruction in the draft. This will need to be corrected before authorization.
